card.name: Highlife
card.tagline: Ghanaian popular music genre with associated social dancing
card.profile: Highlife is a Ghanaian music genre that originated along the coastal cities of present-day Ghana in the 19th century, fusing traditional Akan and Ga melodic/rhythmic structures with Western instruments, jazzy horns and two-finger guitar styles (Wikipedia; Britannica). Primarily a music genre rather than a single codified dance, it is nonetheless a social dance form encouraging individual expression (MoTCCA). It diverged into dance-band and guitar-band streams; Jacob Sam's Kumasi Trio recorded the early highlife 'Yaa Amponsah' in London in June 1928, and E.T. Mensah became the 'King of Highlife' (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Highlife was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity at the 20th session (20.COM) in New Delhi on 10 December 2025 (file No. 02141, 'Highlife music and dance') - Ghana's first UNESCO ICH inscription (UNESCO ICH).

observation.setting: Multiple outdoor and indoor locations including a village dirt clearing, a paved road, a yard with a modern house, and a stage with a band.
observation.dancers: Mixed group of men, women, and children of various ages; dancing solo, in pairs, and in small groups.
observation.formation_and_space: Small groups dancing side by side in lines or clusters, with some solo performers moving freely in open spaces.
observation.posture: Upright torso transitioning frequently into deep knee bends and low squatting stances, with weight shifted actively between feet.
observation.footwork: Rhythmic stepping, stamping, hopping, and bouncing on the beat, with quick foot switches during low squat positions.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held out or bent at the elbows with hand gestures; male dancers in traditional costume wave feathered flywhisks (horsehair whisks).
observation.hips_and_torso: Bouncing torso movements, hip shakes, and deep knee dips with upper body inclinations.
observation.partnering: None; dancers perform side-by-side or solo without physical contact.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Frequent changes between upright standing levels and low squatting levels; occasional small jumps and hops.
observation.costume_and_props: Traditional attire including red caps, beaded necklaces, patterned or fringed skirts, wrappers, and leg wraps; male solo dancers hold feathered flywhisks.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot articulation and weight transfer details are obscured by quick camera cuts and medium-to-wide framing.
